html:
Opobo was a trading city-state in the eastern Niger Delta, in what is now south-eastern Nigeria, founded in 1869 by Jaja. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Jaja was born in Igboland, sold as a boy into slavery in the delta port of Bonny, and rose to head one of its great trading houses. After a civil war in Bonny he moved his followers to a new site, Opobo, which cut Bonny off from the inland markets. Opobo soon controlled much of the region's palm oil trade, and Jaja dealt directly with British firms as its king.

He signed a treaty of protection with Britain in 1884, but refused to let British traders go around him to the inland markets. In 1887 the consul Harry Johnston invited him aboard a ship, arrested him and sent him into exile. Jaja died in 1891 on his way home, and Opobo's trade passed to the British firms.
sum: Opobo was a trading city-state in the eastern Niger Delta, in what is now south-eastern Nigeria, founded in 1869 by Jaja. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.
